source.name: SageMath finite words primitive() and primitive_length()
source.verified_law: primitive root is shortest word u whose positive integer repetition forms w; distinguish minimal_period() which permits incomplete final repetition

source.claim: Repeated radio symbol/framing sequences, without any new RF modem or T5 semantics
Exact p/q oscillator/pulse ratios; library examples, not proven FPGA implementation

selection.behavior: For nonempty finite D1 word w of length n, return the shortest nonempty prefix u of w for which w equals u concatenated exactly n/length(u) times, requiring length(u) divides n; if none shorter exists, return w. Define empty input -> empty output. No floating point, no time or transport effect.
falsifiers: Sage minimal_period(01010) gives 2 by truncated overlap but primitive root is whole word length 5; never use minimal_period naively
Return a lexicographically minimal cyclic rotation (e.g. 0101 -> 01 is coincidence) rather than prefix root, identity invalid
An implementation which accepts a nondivisor p or changes bit order is invalid
selection.dedup_check: Against D1-D9 at 09d1d71c39d1484dfd005a5068dbb18b76f0f0d4 and D10 at a55f307c27f17091795d75ebfcd7d051547d80bc: no exact named law; D8 ROTATE is mutation/rotation and CANONICALIZE generic, neither attests the shortest full-repetition root. Formal equivalence review remains pending.
selection.minimality: A pure mathematical finite-word factorization invariant. It is implementable from comparison, prefix and divisibility; derivability does not imply exclusion, but the universal named root is distinct from a partial overlap period and from a rotation quotient.
